'''Maurice Baker''' (born July 28, 1979) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player. He last played for the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Utah Tech University|Dixie State College]] and [[Oklahoma State University]], and has spent time in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He has also played professionally in Russia, Syria, Mexico, Lithuania, France, Puerto Rico, Philippines, Venezuela, and the Dominican Republic.

Baker played his longest tenure with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], starting with the 2004 season when the team was known as the [[Dakota Wizards]] in the [[Continental Basketball Association]] before the team moved to the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] in 2006. Baker has appeared in the second-most D-League games (356) in league history,<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/santa-cruz-warriors-re-acquire-moe-baker/n-5103781 Santa Cruz Warriors Re-Acquire Moe Baker]</ref> and is the Warriors' franchise all-time leader in points, minutes played, rebounds, assists, steals, and field goals made.<ref name=boxscore>[http://boxscorenews.com/veteran-guard-returns-to-dakota-wizards-p12388-118.htm Veteran Guard Returns To Dakota Wizards]</ref>

==Professional career==
Over his first two professional seasons, between 2002 and 2004, Baker played in Russia, Syria and Mexico. His first stint in the United States came during the 2004–05 season, when he joined the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]]. After averaging 16.9 points, 6.7 assists and 5.4 rebounds in 30 games for Dakota, he was called up to the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in February 2005.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/172405/Clippers-Sign-Baker-Place-Livingston-On-IL Clippers Sign Baker, Place Livingston On IL]</ref> The following month, he garnered another NBA stint, this time with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. Over two 10-day contract periods with the Clippers and Trail Blazers, Baker appeared in five games with limited court time.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bakerma01/gamelog/2005/ Maurice Baker 2004-05 Game Log]</ref>

Baker's 10-day contract with the Trail Blazers ended up being his final playing time in the NBA, as the rest of his professional basketball career was played in the D-League and overseas. His final game was played on March 19, 2005, in a 92 - 97 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]] where he only played for 5 seconds and recorded no stats.

Baker returned to the Dakota Wizards for the 2005–06 season, playing with them until January 2006 when he moved to Lithuania to play for [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos Rytas]]. In 12 [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|league]] games for Rytas, he averaged 6.5 points, 3.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.7 steals per game.

In the summer of 2006, Baker underwent ankle surgery, and was deemed "about 80 percent of the player he was before" the surgery.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=sheridan_chris&page=dleagueshowcases-080118 D-League showcase: Maurice Baker might help a contender at this point]</ref> For the 2006–07 season, Baker returned to the Dakota Wizards, with the team now playing in the [[NBA Development League]]. In their first D-League season, Baker helped the Wizards win the championship, leading the team in rebounds with ten while scoring nineteen points in the Championship game against the [[Texas Legends|Colorado 14ers]].<ref>[http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2014/4/25/5651996/an-ode-to-the-importance-of-nba-d-league-veteran-maurice-baker An Ode to the Importance of NBA D-League Veteran Maurice Baker]</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://scores.nba.com/games/20070429/COLDAK/boxscoreprint.html |title=Boxscore |website=scores.nba.com |access-date=15 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070503090837/http://scores.nba.com/games/20070429/COLDAK/boxscoreprint.html |archive-date=3 May 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He again played for Dakota in 2007–08, departing the team in January 2008 to join [[Paris-Levallois Basket|Paris-Levallois]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].

In 2008–09, Baker again played in the NBA Development League for the Dakota Wizards, earning All-Star honors for the first time.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/allstar2009.html NBA D-League All-Star 2009] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206090725/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/allstar2009.html |date=2016-02-06 }}</ref> Following the season with Dakota, Baker moved to Puerto Rico for the 2009 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season, joining [[Atléticos de San Germán]]. He returned to Dakota for the 2009–10 season, before again playing in Puerto Rico in the off-season, this time joining [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]].

For the 2010–11 season, Baker moved to Mexico where he played for Ola Verde de Poza Rica. In January 2011, he returned to the Dakota Wizards for the rest of the season.<ref name="boxscore" /> He later had stints in the Philippines for the [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]],<ref>[http://www.ballerspinas.com/2011/05/new-import-of-talk-n-text-tropang.html#.Vs05BYx94zY The New Import Of Talk 'n Text Tropang Texters For Governor's Cup 2011: Maurice Baker]</ref> and in Venezuela for [[Guaiqueríes de Margarita]].

Baker again played for the Dakota Wizards in 2011–12. He then played in the Dominican Republic during the 2012 off-season for [[Cañeros del Este]].<ref>[http://www.melvynlopez.com/2012/08/maurice-baker-debuta-hoy-con-caneros.html MAURICE BAKER DEBUTA HOY CON CAÑEROS DEL ESTE] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006030553/http://www.melvynlopez.com/2012/08/maurice-baker-debuta-hoy-con-caneros.html |date=2016-10-06 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[http://elnacional.com.do/caneros-del-este-se-sacuden-ante-metros-santiago/ Cañeros del Este se sacuden ante Metros Santiago] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[http://elnacional.com.do/mario-west-le-da-vida-a-los-caneros-del-este/ Mario West le da vida a  los Cañeros del Este] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

In 2012, the Wizards were moved from [[North Dakota]] to [[California]] by their NBA affiliate team, the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>[http://www.bayareasportsguy.com/dakota-wizards-to-santa-cruz-makes-sense-for-both-the-warriors-and-surf-city/ Dakota Wizards to Santa Cruz? Makes sense for both the Warriors and Surf City]</ref> The team was subsequently renamed the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], and Baker continued on with Santa Cruz. Between 2012 and 2016, Baker was a consistent presence on the Santa Cruz roster, earning his second D-League championship in the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Title Wave: Santa Cruz Wins NBA D-League Championship|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150426/FWNSCW/|accessdate=April 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2015}}</ref>

== Coaching career==
Prior to the start of the [[2022–23 NBA season]], Baker was hired as an assistant coach for the [[Indiana Pacers]] under head coach [[Rick Carlisle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maurice Baker|url=https://nbacoaches.com/maurice-baker/|work=nbacoaches.com|date=October 15, 2022 |accessdate=September 3, 2024}}</ref>
